title: Rufus and the Moonpetal Hunt
markdown:
Gathering things for a very special supper can be quite an adventure, especially for Rufus, a wizard not much taller than his book of spells. He lived with his Grandma high up in their cozy home. Sometimes even the smallest wizards need a very special flower, one that blooms only when the moon is just right.

Twilight. Soft purple and sleepy orange. The air like a blanket. Grandma was making Sleepytime Stew: warm spices, sweet berries. Missing one tiny special thing: a Moonpetal. Moonpetals opened their shiny silver leaves when moonbeams tickled them. They were the secret of the stew, the magic that helped you dream of fluffy clouds and warm cookies.

“Rufus, my little star.” Her voice a warm hug, hands dusted with flour. “Could you fetch a Moonpetal from the woods? Just a few, for my stew.” Eyes twinkling.

Rufus puffed his chest, trying to look as brave as a knight. “Of course, Grandma!” Bright hair bouncing.

And who came running, tail a question mark of excitement? Flicker, his little kitten: fur as soft as moonlight, eyes like two shiny green gems. Flicker loved adventures almost as much as naps in sunny spots. Rufus scooped him up. A purr like a little engine. “You’re coming too. We’ll be a team.”

The woods were not dark or spooky. Ferns, kissed by the early moon, glowed like a thousand tiny friendly lanterns, each one pulsing as if it had a small polite heart. Sweet wet ground after rain, sweet flowers. A rustle of leaves. A far-off hoot of a friendly owl saying hello and then thinking better of a second hoot, because stew-evenings are for quiet. Flicker wiggled, whiskers twitching, safe in Rufus’s arms.

They walked deeper. Fern-light like a path. Rufus hummed a wandering wizard tune, the one Grandma used when the spoon got stuck. Flicker purred, a tiny motor of happiness. Once Rufus thought he saw Moonpetals and it was only frost on a leaf, which was pretty and not stew. He looked again for the silvery gleam, leaves like captured moonlight.

Then: a gentle tap-tap-swish. A yummy smell of fresh bread. Flicker’s ears perked.

A goblin, round and rosy-cheeked, flour on his pointy hat and cheerful nose, stood outside a tiny cottage shaped like a cheerful mushroom. Puzzled. This was Mr. Crumble, the baker. Windowpanes like sparkling dewdrops. Chimney puffing sweet smoke.

He sighed, a puff of flour. “Oh, dear, oh dear.” Tapped a plump loaf. “So many Moonpetals, all baked into my moon-muffins. The best I have ever made! But I needed them for my Midnight Mellow Bars. And now there are none left.” Rosy cheeks a little less bright. He loved making treats for everyone in the woods.

Rufus peeked around a glowing fern. Moonpetals peeked from the warm golden-brown bread. Mr. Crumble looked sad. Rufus felt a little ache. He stepped forward, Flicker on his shoulder.

“Excuse me, Mr. Crumble?”

The goblin jumped, then smiled, the frown chased off. “Well, hello! A young wizard and a moonbeam kitten! Come closer.”

“I’m Rufus. This is Flicker. We need Moonpetals for Grandma’s stew. But I see you need them too.” He looked at the bread, then the worried kind face. “What if Flicker and I helped you find some more special things for your Midnight Mellow Bars? And then, could we please have just a few Moonpetals for Grandma?”

Mr. Crumble’s face lit like a firework. “Ever so helpful! My baking brain gets mixed up. I get so excited about the baking, I forget the collecting. We need sun-spun sugar from the Whispering Willow. And maybe a dewdrop from the Giggle-grass, for sparkle.”

So they set off, Mr. Crumble leading, flour still drifting off his hat like a private weather. The Whispering Willow stood where the ferns grew shy. Rufus used a spark of magic no bigger than a firefly to coax the sun-spun sugar from the branches. It floated down like golden dust and stuck to Flicker’s whiskers, which Flicker considered a salary. Then the Giggle-grass, a patch that shook before anyone touched it, as if it had been waiting for a joke. Flicker, with a kitten pounce and a curious nose, nudged a large shimmering dewdrop into a little leaf-cup. The grass tickled their noses. They all giggled, a silly happy sound that made the owl, far off, risk that second hoot after all.

Back at the mushroom cottage the air was already warm with baking. Mr. Crumble whipped up Midnight Mellow Bars that smelled of honey and sunshine. As promised, he took a handful of shimmering Moonpetals from the bread and placed them in Rufus’s hand. They glowed like little promises.

“Thank you, Rufus.” A warm crescent moon-muffin in the other hand. “You and your feline friend have saved my midnight treats.” He did not make a speech about sharing. He wiped flour on his apron and looked pleased, which was enough.

They waved. He promised cookies next time. Homeward: Moonpetals tucked away, muffin smelling heavenly, fern-light brighter, a path of soft light to the cozy cottage.

Grandma dropped the petals into the stew. It steamed. Flicker got a saucer of the broth, which was not strictly traditional and was strictly allowed. Rufus ate his muffin slowly, so the moon would last. The stew, when they tasted it, did the rest.
